salary_used.note: Salary as entered for 2026, grown to 2027-28 with the OBR average earnings index.

council_tax_used.note: Band B at the region's average Band D for 2026-27, grown to 2027-28 with the OBR's Council Tax forecast.

state_pension_used.note: At State Pension age, the State Pension as entered, or else the full new State Pension for 2027-28.

measures.name: Warm Home Discount top-up
measures.note: If received: the £100 is shown for a household in Great Britain on Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit or income-related ESA in 2026-27. Not every eligible household receives the Warm Home Discount: the national figures pay it to 85% of Pension Credit households and 70% of other eligible households (DESNZ receipt rates).

by_policy.method: Each measure's change is that measure switched to its Budget setting, with every other selected measure held at pre-Budget law, against the same baseline. The combined change switches them all at once. The residual is the combined change minus the sum of the single changes: what the measures do together beyond what each does alone.

programmes.label: Income Tax
programmes.note: Includes the High Income Child Benefit Charge, so Child Benefit is shown before it.

programmes.label: Council Tax
programmes.note: Estimated from the band and the region's average Band D (COUNCIL_TAX_BAND_D), unless entered. No measure changes it.

programmes.label: Fuel duty
programmes.note: From the petrol and diesel spending entered.

programmes.label: VAT
programmes.note: The change in VAT the measures make on the spending entered (electricity, petrol and diesel). The form asks about no other spending, so VAT itself is not shown: £0 before the Budget.

programmes.label: Pension contributions from pay
programmes.note: Not a tax, but taken off net income. Salary sacrificed above the salary sacrifice cap is paid into the pension from pay instead.

programmes.label: Universal Credit
programmes.note: Before the benefit cap, which is its own row. Elements are before the earnings taper.

programmes.label: Housing Benefit
programmes.note: Before the benefit cap, which is its own row.

programmes.label: Benefit cap
programmes.note: What the benefit cap takes off Universal Credit and Housing Benefit, shown as a negative amount, so the rows above it are before the cap and the group adds up to what is paid.

programmes.label: Council Tax Reduction
programmes.note: Where policyengine-uk simulates the scheme that applies: England's pension-age scheme, the Scottish and Welsh schemes, and the working-age schemes of Kingston upon Thames, Merton, Newham, Oxford and Westminster. Elsewhere none is counted.

programmes.label: Warm Home Discount top-up
programmes.note: The candidate £100 more Warm Home Discount in 2026-27, paid through policyengine-uk's cost-of-living payment, for a household in Great Britain on Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Housing Benefit or income-related ESA, if received.

programmes.label: Free childcare hours
programmes.note: The value of the funded hours, which policyengine-uk counts in net income.

programmes.label: Employment income
programmes.note: The £2,000 salary sacrifice cap from April 2029 is existing law (Budget 2025), so it is the same before and after the measures. policyengine-uk assumes employers recover the cap's extra employer National Insurance by cutting every employee's pay by a set share, whether or not they use salary sacrifice: the pay cut row, a negative amount.

children.label: Pay cut for the salary sacrifice cap (current law)

answer.dependants_note: Who counts as a child follows policyengine-uk: everyone under 16, and a 16- to 19-year-old in full-time non-advanced education (school or college) begun before 19. Child Benefit counts such a young person until 20; Universal Credit stops at the 1 September after their 19th birthday, so a 19-year-old counts for Child Benefit but not Universal Credit.

sweep.note: Only the head's employment income varies; everything else is held as entered. A marginal rate is over the interval between two neighbouring points: one minus the change in household net income over the change in the head's employment income. The rate at the head's own income is over the next £200 they earn. net_income_parts splits net income at each point into its parts, in pounds with taxes negative, adding up to it.
